parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
The point P in Fig. 1.1 represents a point mass.
On Fig. 1.1, draw lines to represent the gravitational field due to the point mass P.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Many moons are in circular orbit about a planet.
Explain why the gravitational force on a moon does not do any work on the moon.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text:
Show that the mass $M$ of the planet is given by
$$M = \frac{\text{gradient}}{G}$$
where $G$ is the gravitational constant.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: Use Fig. 1.2 and the expression in (c)(i) to show that the mass $M$ of the planet is $1.0 \times 10^{26}\text{ kg}$.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text:
A moon is in a circular orbit of radius $1.2 \times 10^{8}\text{ m}$ about the planet.
Calculate the linear speed $v$ of this moon.
$$v = \text{...................................................... m s}^{-1}$$
